## The problem

Which routinely collected clinical and laboratory measures carry signal about depression severity, and do different variable-ranking methods agree?

## Approach

NHANES 2017-Mar 2020 pre-pandemic files merged on SEQN; PHQ-9 items modeled with brms cumulative-logit IRT (equal discrimination) to get latent severity; predictors cleaned (NZV, correlation filter, scaling); SIR with GMM-derived slices, PCA, cross-validated LASSO, and XGBoost+SHAP each rank variables; GAMs refit on top-10 variables per method.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Could inform which low-cost measures are worth including in behavioral-health screening or readiness-risk models (e.g., Army H2F/medical readiness), but no decision framing is stated.
:::

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- No NHANES survey weights, strata, or PSUs, so results describe an unweighted sample, not the U.S. population.
- Latent severity scores are computed incorrectly: the row-mean of ranef summary columns (estimate, SE, CI bounds) is used as the posterior mean.
- Variables are selected and evaluated on the same data; the GAM R2 values (0.04-0.12) are in-sample and hard-coded.
- SIR dimension d=10 isn't tested; eigen-decomposition uses a symmetrized Sigma^-1 M; the top loadings reflect the exact collinearity total protein = albumin + globulin.
- Cross-sectional data with no causal interpretation; several top predictors (chronic conditions, activity, income) may be consequences of depression.
- Blanket recoding of 7/9/77/99 values as missing can delete legitimate responses.
- Mean imputation across fasting-subsample labs.

R, brms, cmdstanr, mclust, glmnet, xgboost, SHAPforxgboost, mgcv, caret, gt
